title: A familiar silhouette
text: Look up. Some buildings are so familiar that we forget to really look at them. Here beside Parliament, the clock tower rises above the city. You probably call it Big Ben. But the tower itself is called the Elizabeth Tower. Let's look a little closer.

title: The face of the city
text: Now bring your eyes to the clock face. Notice the hands, the Roman numerals, and the stonework around them. The clock began ticking in May eighteen fifty nine. This familiar landmark is also a working instrument. A way for a whole city to share the time.

title: The name you can hear
text: Follow the tower upwards. The great bell is hidden inside. That is Big Ben. You can see the tower from here, but the name belongs to something you hear. The bell first sounded in July eighteen fifty nine, a few weeks after the clock began its working life.

title: Back to the bigger picture
text: Now take a step back. See how the tower belongs to a much larger building, the Palace of Westminster. Look again at the outline against the sky. The next time you pass, you might notice a little more. And when you are ready, there is another story across Parliament Square, at Westminster Abbey.
